aspects.says: Field 4 is minor units and the currency in field 49 places the decimal point; amounts stay BigDecimal, and only the gateway's own list of currencies is accepted.
basis: section:12.2. An Amount Is Minor Units, and the Currency Says Where the Point Goes

aspects.says: The gateway claims each idempotency key atomically, refuses it for another payment and answers every retry with the stored outcome, failures included, so one key sends at most one 0200.
basis: section:12.5. A Retried Call Carries the Same Idempotency Key, So It Is Applied Once

aspects.says: None of the gateway's error text is copied into the ISO response.
basis: section:12.4. A Value With No Entry in the Table Is Refused, Never Guessed
aspects.reason: a rule about what to leave out of free-text fields; the mapping practice's refusals and the quiz cover the table it belongs to, and a test could only check one invented message

aspects.says: Each endpoint maps into one internal format of full values and out of it, so a new endpoint adds one mapping and each decision about amounts, dates and codes is taken once.
basis: section:12.1. Each Endpoint Maps Into One Internal Format and Out of It

aspects.says: Processing codes map on their transaction type through an explicit table, and a type the table lacks is refused rather than sent as a sale.
basis: section:12.4. A Value With No Entry in the Table Is Refused, Never Guessed

aspects.says: As a REST client, the switch repeats a timed-out call with the same key to learn its outcome, and a new attempt after a stored failure needs a new key.
basis: section:12.5. A Retried Call Carries the Same Idempotency Key, So It Is Applied Once

aspects.says: A gateway status the reply table lacks gets 96 and a cancellation at the gateway, since it may have been an approval.
basis: section:12.4. A Value With No Entry in the Table Is Refused, Never Guessed

aspects.says: ISO 8583 keeps the memory of an unknown outcome on the sender, which reverses; REST with keys keeps it on the receiver, which answers retries.
basis: section:12.9. Design Note: Why REST Retries and ISO 8583 Reverses
aspects.reason: a design essay comparing two protocols; its consequences are graded through the idempotency practice

aspects.says: A date without a year takes the year that puts it nearest to a clock passed in, so a delayed advice keeps last year and a fast terminal's message at New Year gets the new one.
basis: section:12.3. A Date Without a Year Takes the Year Nearest to the Clock You Pass In
